evidenceAudit.scope: Community follow-up after PCI for acute coronary syndrome, including antiplatelet safety, risk-factor treatment and rehabilitation.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi post-PCI community guideline was opened.
Exact antiplatelet choice and duration depend on the PCI discharge plan, bleeding risk and any anticoagulation indication.

pathophysiology.summary: Stented coronary segments remain vulnerable to platelet-mediated thrombosis, especially when antiplatelet therapy is interrupted. Atherosclerosis persists outside the treated lesion. Left-ventricular dysfunction after infarction increases heart-failure and arrhythmic risk. Rehabilitation and risk-factor control reduce recurrent cardiovascular events.

symptoms: Exertional chest pain, breathlessness, bleeding, medication adverse effects or reduced exercise tolerance.
physicalSigns: Blood-pressure abnormality, congestion, access-site complication, anaemia or bradycardia.
redFlags: Rest pain or recurrent acute coronary syndrome symptoms, syncope, pulmonary oedema, major bleeding or abrupt antiplatelet interruption.
precipitants: Missed antiplatelet doses, smoking, uncontrolled BP or lipids, drug interaction and untreated diabetes.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: New ischaemic pain or ECG change is an emergency, not a routine medication review.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Antiplatelet, statin, ACE inhibitor and beta-blocker plan
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Resolve against the interventional-cardiology discharge plan before changing treatment.
ruleIn.normalValue: All discharge medicines and durations reconciled

ruleIn.testName: Blood pressure, renal function and electrolytes
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Hypotension, creatinine change or potassium abnormality
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Check before and 1–2 weeks after initiation or dose increases.
ruleIn.normalValue: Within patient-specific target and local laboratory range

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Urgent hospital assessment for new ischaemic symptoms.
ruleOut.normalValue: No new ischaemic or rhythm change

clinicalManagement.title: Reconcile discharge plan
actions: Confirm stent/ACS indication, antiplatelet agents, planned stop dates, anticoagulation and bleeding risk.
Do not interrupt antiplatelet therapy without urgent discussion with the PCI team unless managing life-threatening bleeding.

clinicalManagement.title: Optimise secondary prevention
actions: Titrate ACE inhibitor and beta-blocker per discharge plan and monitor BP, renal function and electrolytes.
Continue high-intensity statin and address smoking, diabetes, weight and physical activity.

clinicalManagement.title: Cardiac rehabilitation
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Start as soon as possible; first session within 10 days of discharge after MI
actions: Confirm referral and remove transport, language or scheduling barriers.
Escalate recurrent angina, heart failure, syncope, major bleeding or medication intolerance.

medicationPlan.note: Continue the PCI discharge antiplatelet and secondary-prevention regimen exactly as documented. This topic does not invent a universal post-PCI regimen because stent indication, ACS status, bleeding risk and anticoagulation change drug choice and duration.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Continue for up to 12 months unless contraindicated; follow the PCI discharge plan.

teaching.scope: Community follow-up after PCI for acute coronary syndrome, including antiplatelet safety, risk-factor treatment and rehabilitation.
learningObjectives: Identify urgent ischaemic and bleeding complications.
pitfalls: Stopping an antiplatelet without the PCI team.
Missing an anticoagulant-antiplatelet interaction or triple-therapy bleeding risk.
keyPoints: Publication is not permission to alter the PCI discharge plan.
Cardiac rehabilitation starts early and includes exercise and education.

patientEducation: Give written antiplatelet stop dates and emergency advice for chest pain and bleeding.
lifestyleAndDiet: Smoking cessation, Mediterranean-style diet, graded activity through rehabilitation and weight management.
mdtReferrals: Interventional cardiology, cardiac rehabilitation, pharmacy, primary care and anticoagulation service.
dischargeCriteria: Community pathway remains appropriate when clinically stable, medicines are reconciled and no recurrent ischaemia, heart failure or major bleeding is present.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review early after discharge, again during titration, and at least annually for symptoms, bleeding, adherence and cardiovascular risk factors.
